trigger: After the unconstrained replay showed that better average DINO similarity can coincide with more rejected digital frames, test an explicit outage constraint. This is a post-hoc development extension. Keep the original deterministic split; the same 50 evaluation sources have already been inspected in aggregate.
action_and_feedback: Keep the 300 NeST actions and two bits every two slots, received after two slots. Include every action's measured rejection or paid NULL. Both ends know the schedule/report and can reproduce a public randomized action draw independent of channel and image. Report expectations under that randomization; no new physical packets or receiver invocations.
calibration: For each p_design in [0.60,0.95] and cap in [0.01,0.05], maximize calibration-source expected DINO cosine over mixtures of actions for each feedback symbol and phase. Require each action-mixture row to sum to one and global expected rejection-or-NULL probability to be <= cap, averaged over the stationary state, report, phase and 50 calibration images. Use scipy.optimize.linprog(method='highs'). This is a mean-risk constraint under the design law, not a per-report bound or finite-sample reliability certificate.
evaluation: Freeze nonzero mixture weights on the calibration side. Apply each table both to its design persistence and the opposite persistence, without updating decisions. Evaluate raw scores of the other 50 images; report absolute values and direct source-bootstrap differences from the original static and unconstrained two-every-two policies calibrated at the design p. Keep mismatches and cap overshoots. No constraint fitting or action reselection based on evaluation images.
